9-panel cinematic storyboard sheet derived from Image 1. Mix Wide, Medium, and Tight shots of the same scene. No borders between panels.

Layout: 3x3 grid (9 panels) in a 16:9 landscape image.

Scene: Cinematic wide shot, locked-off frame from the very back of a small basement comedy club, editorial social-first campaign energy. SCARLETT VEGA (Image 2) stands centered on a black scuffed stage in her fitted black cotton turtleneck with sleeves pushed up to the elbows, dark slim jeans and scuffed black ankle boots, small gold hoop earrings catching the light and a thin silver ring on her right index finger, her jacket and canvas tote left off-stage. She has just lifted the microphone free of the chrome mic stand, one hand tight around the mic body, cable dangling and swinging, her body leaning in toward it as laughter breaks over her — head tipping back, mouth wide open, shoulders shaking, weight shifted onto the back foot, the empty stand tilted slightly beside her, a wooden stool at the edge of the light. Exposed warm red-brown brick back wall behind her, mortar lines and chipped paint texture picking up spill from the beam. Between camera and stage, rows of silhouetted audience heads at tiny round cabaret tables in the foreground, small candle glasses glowing amber as soft out-of-focus points across the raked room, low ceiling and ductwork barely visible in blackness. Lighting is a single hard front spotlight carving a clean cone around her, hot white on her face and chest with punchy flash-like contrast, deep crushed black surround, faint haze and dust drifting in the beam, the glossy coral of her lips the only saturated accent in the frame. Shot on a 35mm anamorphic lens from the rear of the room at eye level, slight compression through the crowd silhouettes, foreground heads soft and out of focus, sharp on the stage, subtle horizontal flare off the spotlight, fine 35mm grain, crisp true-to-life color with warm highlights and lifted-but-moody shadows, 16:9.

Every panel is a shot of the same scene as Image 1 — keep the characters, wardrobe, lighting, color grade, and texture consistent across all panels.

No text, dialogue bubbles, scene numbers, or watermarks.

Reference images define identity — keep every referenced character, object, and location consistent with its reference image; never render a reference image itself as a separate panel or subject.
